table.title: [val][adversarial] Long group header over tiny sub-columns
table.html:

understanding.purpose: Compare benchmark accuracy across three model sizes and three language subsets, with notes providing context for each result.
understanding.reading: Readers scan down each language column to compare model sizes, across each row to compare languages, and then consult the notes for context.
groups: EN, ZH, and AR are parallel accuracy measures under one shared benchmark header; equal widths support comparison.
Model identifies each row, while Notes supplies supporting prose for that row.
keep_intact: Language identifiers EN, ZH, and AR
Words in the benchmark header and notes
may_wrap: The shared benchmark header can wrap between words across the three metric columns.
Notes can wrap naturally; their row heights can also accommodate any wrapping elsewhere in the row.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Refine r1A by shifting 3px from the metric group to Notes. This tests whether the prose can gain space while the shared header remains at three lines.

preferred.name: r2B
preferred.note: Test the midpoint between r1A and r1C to find whether a wider Notes column can coexist with a three-line shared header.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Use an intermediate allocation between r0A and r0B, giving the shared heading more room while returning 20px to Notes compared with r0B.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Make a smaller shift from Notes to the accuracy group than in the balanced option, preserving much of r0A's readable note wrapping while testing a slightly wider heading.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Try a middle ground that gives Notes 12px more than r2B while retaining more room for the shared benchmark header.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Refine r2B with a modest transfer to Notes, testing whether a useful line-break threshold can be reached without materially narrowing the metric group.

bad.name: r2C
bad.note: Test a modestly wider metric group than r1A while retaining more Notes width than r1B. This may improve the shared header's phrasing without forcing the Small note to four lines.
bad.why: The first note leaves “CPU.” alone on a fourth line, creating an avoidable orphan and increasing the height of that row.

bad.name: r3A
bad.note: Give Notes substantially more space while keeping the three metric columns equal and wide enough for their labels and values. Check whether the shared header remains balanced and the first note becomes shorter.
bad.why: The narrow benchmark group forces its heading onto five lines, splitting “held-out” across lines and leaving “(%)” alone. The header becomes disproportionately tall.

rationale: The three accuracy columns have matching roles and short values, so equal widths make comparison easy. In r2A and r2B, their combined width gives the group heading three lines while leaving enough room for the longest note to fit in three lines. Model names remain intact, and the notes retain enough width to read as prose. The two preferred designs look effectively equivalent at this scale.

general: Columns with the same role benefit from consistent widths when their contents have similar spatial needs.
A spanning heading needs enough combined width to establish its group clearly, even when the values beneath it are short.
Judge width changes by their effect on meaningful line breaks and row rhythm, not table height alone.
specific: The long benchmark heading and the first note compete for the same limited width.
The preferred ranges describe the tested allocations together: use equal accuracy columns of 58–59px, with the corresponding notes width adjusted to keep the total at 445px.

tradeoffs: A designer may prefer the wider notes column in r1C or r3C despite the extra line in the group heading, or prefer the more spacious accuracy columns in r1B despite the longer first data row.
uncertain: The preferred range is supported by the rendered candidates at 58px and 59px for each accuracy column; untested intermediate allocations or changes to the model column could also be equally good.

critique.good: The equal accuracy columns form a clear comparison group, and the notes remain readable in relatively short blocks. Model names, language labels, and values stay intact.
critique.problems: The shared heading occupies four lines, making the header tall relative to the data. The notes column has ample space while the accuracy group feels compressed.
critique.cause: The three 55px metric columns provide only 165px combined for the long group heading; the 220px Notes column receives nearly half the table width.

critique.good: The wider accuracy group gives the shared heading a more compact three-line shape and makes the three language columns easy to distinguish. The equal metric widths reinforce their parallel roles.
critique.problems: The first note wraps to four lines, making its row disproportionately tall and spreading the comparison values apart. The narrow notes also make the prose feel cramped.
critique.cause: The three 70px metric columns take 210px together, leaving only 170px for Notes.

critique.good: The generous notes column makes the supporting prose easy to scan, and the equal metric columns keep the language comparisons orderly.
critique.problems: The shared heading wraps into five lines and dominates the table. The tiny metric columns make the accuracy group look squeezed between Model and Notes.
critique.cause: The three 45px metric columns offer only 135px combined for the long heading, while Notes takes 250px.

critique.good: The equal metric columns make EN, ZH, and AR easy to compare. The shared header fits in three lines, and the notes remain readable without breaking words. Rows have a reasonably compact rhythm.
critique.problems: The Small row is much taller than the Base row, while the Notes column takes nearly half the table. That allocation is justified by the prose, though it leaves relatively generous space around the short accuracy values.
critique.cause: The 205px Notes column wraps the Small note to three lines; the three 60px metric columns give the shared header enough combined width to stay at three lines.

critique.good: The equal metric columns give the language measures a clear, consistent rhythm, and the shared header fits in three lines.
critique.problems: The Small note becomes a four-line block, creating a conspicuously tall row and weakening the table's vertical rhythm. The extra metric width does little for the short values.
critique.cause: Increasing each metric column to 65px leaves only 190px for Notes, forcing an extra line in the Small note.

critique.good: The wider Notes column gives the prose more breathing room, and the equal metric widths preserve the comparison structure.
critique.problems: The shared header wraps to four lines, making the header block disproportionately tall. The wider Notes column does not reduce the visible Small or Large notes below three and two lines respectively.
critique.cause: The three 57px metric columns provide too little combined width for the shared header to retain its three-line wrap.

critique.good: The three equal metric columns make comparisons easy, and the shared header reads as a coherent group. Model names, values, and notes remain intact; each row reads as a unit.
critique.problems: The metric columns have more space than their short labels and values need, while the long first note still takes three lines.
critique.cause: At 59px each, the metric columns consume 177px, leaving 208px for Notes.

critique.good: Like r2A, this preserves a clear metric group and readable row labels. The slightly wider Notes column maintains the same three-line maximum without splitting words.
critique.problems: The 3px shift to Notes produces no visible improvement over r2A; the first note remains the dominant source of row height.
critique.cause: Reducing each metric column from 59px to 58px does not free enough width to change the note's line breaks.

critique.good: The equal metric columns preserve the comparison structure, and the shared header remains readable in three lines.
critique.problems: The first note falls to four lines, making the first data row visibly taller and leaving more empty space alongside its values.
critique.cause: Increasing each metric column to 62px reduces Notes to 199px, which forces an additional line in the first note.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r2C.why: The three accuracy columns are balanced and the group header reads comfortably. Notes have enough room, though the first note takes four lines.

r1C.why: The wider notes column keeps the first note to three lines, but the group header wraps to four lines and the accuracy columns feel compressed.

r2A.why: The group header fits in three lines, the accuracy columns remain balanced, and the notes read comfortably in three lines or fewer.

r1B.why: The group header and numeric columns are clear, but the narrower notes column makes the first note four lines tall.

ref_equal.why: The accuracy columns are disproportionately wide while the notes column is squeezed into a very narrow measure, producing excessive wrapping and tall rows.

ref_auto.why: The header and accuracy columns are clear, but the notes column is narrow enough to make the first note four lines tall.

raw.unsure: A, D, and F are close in quality; their small differences in column widths have limited practical effect.

r1C.why: The notes have room to read comfortably and the language columns are balanced, though the group header wraps to four lines.

ref_auto.why: The group header fits in three lines and the language columns are even, but the narrower notes column makes the first row four lines tall.

r2C.why: The header and notes are readable, with balanced language columns; the first note takes four lines.

r1B.why: The group header fits neatly in three lines, and the language columns are balanced, though the first note needs four lines.

ref_equal.why: The notes column is extremely narrow, breaking the first note into many short lines and making its row disproportionately tall.

r2A.why: The group header and first note each fit in three lines, while the language columns remain balanced and easy to compare.

raw.unsure: B, C and D are very similar; their small differences in column width have little effect on readability.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
